newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate eases on election results.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate eases on election results.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down a moderate 15 basis points at 19.60 percent in early trade on Tuesday.

Dealers said paper was still in demand on a fresh wave of confidence following Sunday's peaceful mid-term elections. Nonetheless, demand had slowed ahead of Wednesday's cut-off date for banks to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts held with the central bank.
"The heavy demand we saw on Monday has slowed down because of the cut-off date," a dealers said.
Mexicans voted on Sunday for the entire lower house of Congress, one quarter of the Senate, several state governors and, for the first time in modern history, a mayor for the capital.
Preliminary results MEX45 gave Cuauhtmoc Crdenas, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) a 22-point lead in the historic Mexico City race.

The latest count MEX46 meanwhile indicated the Institutional Revolutionary Party could lose control of the lower chamber for the first time since its founding in 1929. Final results are expected on Wednesday.

Fixed-income analysts said that despite liquidity pressures in the market, primary Cetes rates were still expected to fall at the weekly auction later today, as secondary rates had fallen since last week.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile risen 65 basis points to 20.25 percent, after an anomalous close on Monday had placed them below governments.
Liquidity of 148 million pesos was due to return to the system during the session from prior central bank operations.
